newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jilin Chemical to offer A shares.
newsitem.headline: Jilin Chemical to offer A shares.

text.p: Jilin Chemical Industry Co Ltd said on Friday it had been given approval to issue 30 million A shares through the Shenzhen bourse's automated quotation system on September 24 and list them in Shenzhen.

The issue has been priced at 3.50 yuan a share, giving a price-earnings ratio of 14 times based on per-share net earnings of 0.25 yuan on a weighted basis recorded last year, the company said in a prospectus in the official Securities Times.
The firm said the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has also approved a simultaneous offer of 20 million staff shares at the same price.
A spokesman for Jilin Chemical told the China Securities Bulletin the employee stock would not be listed until six months after the the A shares are listed.
Zhongxing Securities has been named the lead underwriter for the offers, the prospectus said.
Jilin Chemical has total share capital of 3.4 billion shares, comprising 2.4 billion state shares and 964.8 million H shares, it said.

The company plans to use proceeds from the issues toward construction of a project slated to produce 300,000 tonnes of polyethylene annually. Trial operations should begin by the end of this year and normal operations in early 1997, the prospectus said.
The spokesman said the firm had invested the bulk of proceeds from its H share offer in the same project. Jilin Chemical issued the H shares at HK$1.589 per share last May, he said.

Jilin Chemical, based in the city of Jilin in northeastern Jilin province, said it posted after-tax profits of 742.62 million yuan in 1995, compared with 555.89 million yuan a year earlier and 647.20 million yuan in 1994.
The firm did not say whether the annual results were compiled under Chinese or international accounting standards.
